angle: Attacks on explanations and robustness of explanations, plus adversarial/evasion attacks specific to traffic classifiers (XAI for network traffic classification)
sources_used: Semantic Scholar Graph API (paper/search with abstracts)
arXiv API (search_query and id_list for verified abstracts)
WebSearch (Slack/Severi/Ghorbani/Dombrowski clusters, problem-space NIDS, encrypted-traffic evasion, IDSGAN)
hbaniecki/adversarial-explainable-ai curated GitHub list (canonical links to the attacks-on-explanations sub-literature)
notes_on_source_yield: OpenAlex returned persistent HTTP 429 with a multi-hour Retry-After for this IP and was dropped. Semantic Scholar's unauthenticated pool rate-limited hard; one rich 40-paper batch (with abstracts) was captured before it throttled. arXiv id_list batching (10 ids per call) was the most reliable way to pull verified abstracts. All classic-hub arXiv ids were title-verified in the feed before inclusion; none were assumed.

papers.title: Fooling LIME and SHAP: Adversarial Attacks on Post hoc Explanation Methods
papers.authors: Dylan Slack, Sophie Hilgard, Emily Jia, Sameer Singh, Himabindu Lakkaraju
papers.venue: AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society (AIES)
papers.relevance: The seminal 'scaffolding' attack showing perturbation-based explainers LIME and SHAP can be reliably fooled to hide a biased classifier; the reference attack for all explanation-manipulation work in security.

papers.title: Interpretation of Neural Networks is Fragile
papers.authors: Amirata Ghorbani, Abubakar Abid, James Zou
papers.relevance: Shows imperceptible input perturbations can drastically change saliency/feature-importance while keeping the prediction; Hessian-geometry analysis argues fragility may be fundamental to gradient explanations.

papers.title: Explanations can be manipulated and geometry is to blame
papers.authors: Ann-Kathrin Dombrowski, Maximillian Alber, Christopher J. Anders, et al.
papers.relevance: Arbitrarily reshapes explanation maps via imperceptible perturbations that keep outputs fixed, attributing the vulnerability to large network curvature (geometry) and proposing smoothing/soft-plus fixes.

papers.title: Fooling Neural Network Interpretations via Adversarial Model Manipulation
papers.authors: Juyeon Heo, Sunghwan Joo, Taesup Moon
papers.relevance: Attacks the model rather than the input: fine-tunes weights so interpretations (Grad-CAM, LRP) become misleading while accuracy is preserved; fooling transfers across explanation methods.

papers.title: Interpretable Deep Learning under Fire (ADV^2)
papers.authors: Xinyang Zhang, Ningfei Wang, Hua Shen, Shouling Ji, Xiapu Luo, Ting Wang
papers.relevance: First systematic security study of interpretable DL systems; ADV2 crafts inputs that simultaneously fool the classifier and its coupled interpreter, identifying the 'prediction-interpretation gap' as root cause.

papers.title: Explanation-Guided Backdoor Poisoning Attacks Against Malware Classifiers
papers.authors: Giorgio Severi, Jim Meyer, Scott Coull, Alina Oprea
papers.relevance: Turns SHAP explanations into an attack tool: uses feature-attribution to pick clean-label backdoor triggers for EMBER/Drebin/Contagio malware classifiers; canonical 'explanation-guided attack' in security.

papers.title: Black Box Attacks on Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods in Cyber Security
papers.authors: Aditya Kuppa, Nhien-An Le-Khac
papers.relevance: One of the first to attack XAI specifically in the cyber-security setting, showing gradient-based explanations of security classifiers can be manipulated in black-box conditions.

papers.title: Disguising Attacks with Explanation-Aware Backdoors
papers.authors: Maximilian Noppel, Lukas Peter, Christian Wressnegger
papers.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P)
papers.relevance: Backdoors that not only flip predictions but also produce an attacker-chosen, benign-looking explanation, defeating explanation-based inspection/audit defenses.

papers.title: SoK: Explainable Machine Learning in Adversarial Environments
papers.authors: Maximilian Noppel, Christian Wressnegger
papers.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P)
papers.relevance: Systematization-of-knowledge that organizes threat models and attacks against explanations in security settings; a taxonomy hub for this angle and a source of open-problem statements.

papers.title: Adversarial attacks and defenses in explainable artificial intelligence: A survey
papers.authors: Hubert Baniecki, Przemyslaw Biecek
papers.relevance: The field-defining survey of adversarial XAI, with unified notation/taxonomy over attacks on explanations and defenses; the best single map for citation expansion on this angle.

papers.title: Explainability Guided Adversarial Evasion Attacks on Malware Detectors
papers.authors: Kshitiz Aryal, Maanak Gupta, Mahmoud Abdelsalam, et al.
papers.relevance: Uses SHAP to locate decision-critical regions of PE malware and injects perturbations there, showing explanation-guided perturbation is far more efficient than random placement for evasion.

papers.title: Revealing the Vulnerabilities of Learning-based Network Intrusion Detectors through XAI-guided Adversarial Attack
papers.authors: Li et al.
papers.relevance: Bullseye: uses SHAP and LIME to guide efficient adversarial traffic generation against learning-based NIDS, directly linking explanation attribution to evasion of traffic classifiers.

papers.title: Explainable But Vulnerable: Adversarial Attacks on XAI Explanation in Cybersecurity Applications
papers.authors: Maraz Mia, et al.
papers.venue: IEEE TPS-ISA (Trust, Privacy and Security in Intelligent Systems and Applications)
papers.relevance: Systematically studies fairwashing, manipulation, and backdoor attacks on SHAP, LIME and Integrated Gradients specifically in cybersecurity classifiers.

papers.title: FATFI: A Framework to Generate Adversarial Traffic with Feature Interpretability
papers.authors: (Springer chapter)
papers.relevance: Bullseye: multi-level (global+local) explanation methods score feature importance to choose optimal perturbation strategies for generating adversarial network traffic.

papers.title: Investigating the Impact of Adversarial Evasion Attacks on Model Explanation in IoT-based DDoS Detection Systems
papers.authors: Mahmood et al.
papers.venue: International Journal of Innovative Science & Technology (IJIST)
papers.relevance: Measures how adversarial evasion perturbations degrade the consistency/stability of SHAP-LIME explanations in IoT DDoS detectors -- attack-on-explanation in the traffic domain.

papers.title: Evaluation of Explainable Artificial Intelligence in IoT Intrusion Detection Systems Under DeepFool Adversarial Conditions
papers.authors: Munilla et al.
papers.relevance: Benchmarks SHAP and LIME robustness for IoT IDS under DeepFool attacks, quantifying trade-offs in feature alignment and explanation stability.

papers.title: Explainable AI-Based Intrusion Detection Systems for Industry 5.0 and Adversarial XAI: A Systematic Review
papers.authors: (MDPI Information systematic review)
papers.relevance: Systematic review at the exact intersection: XAI-based IDS plus 'adversarial XAI', surveying how explanations for traffic/security classifiers are attacked and defended.

papers.title: Are Explanations Robust to Federated Poisoning? An Empirical Study in Cyber Threat Detection
papers.authors: Bakhtiari et al.
papers.venue: SECRYPT (Int. Conf. on Security and Cryptography)
papers.relevance: Studies how federated poisoning attacks degrade the reliability of Integrated Gradients, SHAP and LIME across cyber-threat detection models.

papers.title: IDSGAN: Generative Adversarial Networks for Attack Generation against Intrusion Detection
papers.authors: Zilong Lin, Yong Shi, Zhi Xue
papers.relevance: Foundational GAN that transforms malicious flow records into adversarial traffic evading black-box IDS while preserving attack functionality via a restricted-modification mechanism.

papers.title: Investigating the practicality of adversarial evasion attacks on network intrusion detection
papers.authors: Mohamed Amine Merzouk, Frederic Cuppens, Nora Boulahia-Cuppens, Reda Yaich
papers.relevance: Argues classic adversarial-example algorithms produce unrealizable traffic (boolean/discrete features, out-of-range values), a key statement of the feature-space vs problem-space gap for NIDS.

papers.title: Evasion Adversarial Attacks Remain Impractical Against ML-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems, Especially Dynamic Ones
papers.authors: Mohamed elShehaby, Ashraf Matrawy
papers.relevance: Threat-models practicality of evasion against ML-NIDS and shows continuous retraining (dynamic learning) sharply cuts attack effectiveness -- a strong research-vs-practice-gap statement.

papers.title: Problem space structural adversarial attacks for Network Intrusion Detection Systems based on Graph Neural Networks
papers.authors: Andrea Venturi, et al.
papers.relevance: Formalizes problem-space constraints for GNN-based NIDS; finds GNNs resist feature-based attacks but remain vulnerable to structure-based (graph-topology) perturbations.

papers.title: A Novel Perturb-ability Score to Mitigate Evasion Adversarial Attacks on Flow-Based ML-NIDS
papers.authors: Mohamed elShehaby, Ashraf Matrawy
papers.relevance: Defines a per-feature 'perturb-ability' score to identify which flow features an attacker can realistically manipulate, using it to harden flow-based NIDS -- feature-realism defense.

papers.title: PLAA: Packet-level Adversarial Attacks in Network Traffic Detection
papers.authors: You et al.
papers.relevance: Constructs packet-level adversarial traffic that preserves validity and semantic integrity, reporting ~92.8% average evasion across datasets -- a realistic problem-space traffic attack.

papers.title: Controllability-Aware Adversarial Examples Against LLM-Based Network Traffic Classifiers
papers.authors: Li et al.
papers.relevance: Black-box transfer attack that partitions flow features by attacker controllability to evade emerging LLM-based traffic classifiers; shows LLM classifiers carry substantial transfer vulnerability.

papers.title: Evaluating Resilience of Encrypted Traffic Classification Against Adversarial Evasion Attacks
papers.authors: Ramy Maarouf, et al.
papers.relevance: Tests ML and DL encrypted-traffic classifiers against ZOO, PGD and DeepFool evasion, finding DL is generally more resilient than classical ML -- direct traffic-classifier robustness evaluation.

papers.title: Review on the Feasibility of Adversarial Evasion Attacks and Defenses for Network Intrusion Detection Systems
papers.authors: Islam Debicha, Benjamin Cochez, Tayeb Kenaza, Thibault Debatty, Jean-Michel Dricot, Wim Mees
papers.relevance: Survey of the feasibility of evasion attacks/defenses specific to NIDS; good background hub for the adversarial-traffic half of the angle.

papers.title: TAD: Transfer learning-based multi-adversarial detection of evasion attacks against network intrusion detection systems
papers.authors: Islam Debicha, Richard Bauwens, Thibault Debatty, Jean-Michel Dricot, Tayeb Kenaza, Wim Mees
papers.relevance: Defense that stacks multiple transfer-learned detectors to catch adversarial evasion traffic against NIDS.

papers.title: Defending network intrusion detection systems against adversarial evasion attacks
papers.authors: Marek Pawlicki, Michal Choras, Rafal Kozik
papers.relevance: Early defense study detecting adversarial evasion at NIDS inference time; frequently cited baseline for the adversarial-NIDS thread.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning based Evasion Generative Adversarial Network for Botnet Detection
papers.authors: Rizwan Hamid Randhawa, et al.
papers.relevance: Combines DRL with a GAN to generate semantics-preserving evasion traffic against botnet detectors, converging faster within functional constraints.

papers.title: Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
papers.authors: Julius Adebayo, Justin Gilmer, Michael Muelly, Ian Goodfellow, Moritz Hardt, Been Kim
papers.relevance: Shows some saliency methods are insensitive to model/data randomization, motivating the whole reliability/robustness-of-explanations line that the attacks exploit.

papers.title: Robust Attribution Regularization
papers.authors: Jiefeng Chen, Xi Wu, Vaibhav Rastogi, Yingyu Liang, Somesh Jha
papers.relevance: Training objective that makes Integrated Gradients attributions robust to input perturbation; a canonical defense against attribution attacks.

papers.title: Fairwashing Explanations with Off-Manifold Detergent
papers.authors: Christopher J. Anders, Plamen Pasliev, Ann-Kathrin Dombrowski, Klaus-Robert Muller, Pan Kessel
papers.relevance: Demonstrates two same-accuracy classifiers can be made to yield arbitrary (fairwashed) explanations by exploiting off-manifold behavior; proposes a manifold-based robustness fix.

papers.title: Smoothed Geometry for Robust Attribution
papers.authors: Zifan Wang, Haofan Wang, Shakul Ramkumar, Matt Fredrikson, Piotr Mardziel, Anupam Datta
papers.relevance: Derives Lipschitz/geometry conditions under which gradient attributions are robust and regularizes for them; complements Dombrowski's geometry diagnosis with a defense.

papers.title: Certifiably robust interpretation via Renyi differential privacy
papers.authors: Ao Liu, Xiaoyu Chen, Sijia Liu, Lirong Xia, Chuang Gan
papers.relevance: Provides certified robustness guarantees for feature-attribution explanations using Renyi differential privacy -- the certification angle for explanation robustness.

papers.title: Robust Explanation Constraints for Neural Networks
papers.authors: Matthew Wicker, Juyeon Heo, Luca Costabello, Adrian Weller
papers.relevance: Trains networks with certified constraints so gradient explanations provably cannot be moved outside a set by bounded perturbations -- explanation-robustness certification.

papers.title: Is your explanation stable? A Robustness Evaluation Framework for Feature Attribution
papers.authors: Yuyou Gan, Yuhao Mao, Xuhong Zhang, Shouling Ji, et al.
papers.relevance: Proposes Median Test for Feature Attribution to statistically evaluate whether an explanation is stable under adversarial perturbation -- a robustness-evaluation methodology.

papers.title: Counterfactual Explanations Can Be Manipulated
papers.authors: Dylan Slack, Sophie Hilgard, Himabindu Lakkaraju, Sameer Singh
papers.relevance: Extends explanation-manipulation to counterfactual/recourse explanations, showing models can be built to give unfairly cheap recourse to chosen subgroups.

papers.title: Fooling SHAP with Stealthily Biased Sampling
papers.authors: Gabriel Laberge, Ulrich Aivodji, Satoshi Hara, Mario Marchand, Foutse Khomh
papers.relevance: Manipulates SHAP global explanations by biasing the background sampling distribution rather than the model -- a data-side attack on Shapley explanations.

papers.title: Fooling Partial Dependence via Data Poisoning
papers.authors: Hubert Baniecki, Wojciech Kretowicz, Przemyslaw Biecek
papers.relevance: Poisons data to arbitrarily bend Partial Dependence Plots using genetic and gradient algorithms -- extends explanation manipulation to global model-agnostic explanations.

papers.title: Foiling Explanations in Deep Neural Networks
papers.authors: Snir Vitrack Tamam, Raz Lapid, Moshe Sipper
papers.relevance: AttaXAI: a black-box, query-only evolution-strategy attack that manipulates image explanations without model access -- shows attacks work without gradients.

papers.title: Fooling SHAP with Output Shuffling Attacks
papers.authors: Jun Yuan, et al.
papers.relevance: Introduces data-agnostic output-shuffling attacks that evade Shapley-value bias detection, broadening the catalog of SHAP-specific attacks.

papers.title: XAI-Guided Physical Adversarial Machine Learning Attacks on Automatic Modulation Classification
papers.authors: Salmi et al.
papers.venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications (JSAC)
papers.relevance: Uses SHAP and Grad-CAM++ to guide FGSM-style physical adversarial attacks on RF/modulation classifiers, outperforming non-XAI attacks -- explanation-guided evasion of a signal/traffic classifier.

papers.title: SFA-IoT: segment-to-flow aligned adversarial defense for interpretable IoT device identification
papers.authors: Hussini et al.
papers.relevance: Adversarial purification for interpretable IoT device/traffic identification, restoring accuracy under FGSM/PGD while using SHAP/LIME as diagnostic guidance.

papers.title: Additive Feature Attribution Explainable Methods to Craft Adversarial Attacks for Text Classification and Text Regression
papers.authors: Yidong Chai, et al.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (TKDE)
papers.relevance: Explanation-guided attack: uses LIME/SHAP token attributions to select high-sensitivity tokens for black-box text adversarial attacks -- same recipe applied to sequence classifiers.

papers.title: SHLIME: Foiling adversarial attacks fooling SHAP and LIME
papers.authors: Chauhan et al.
papers.relevance: Ensemble defense that restores bias detection under Slack-style scaffolding attacks on SHAP/LIME -- a direct defensive counterpart to the seminal attack.

papers.title: Comprehensive Survey on Adversarial Examples in Cybersecurity: Impacts, Challenges, and Mitigation Strategies
papers.authors: (arXiv survey)
papers.relevance: Broad survey of adversarial examples across cyber-security domains (malware, NIDS, spam), useful for situating traffic-classifier attacks in the wider threat landscape.

papers.title: A Lightweight, Efficient and Explainable-by-Design Convolutional Neural Network for Internet Traffic Classification (LEXNet)
papers.authors: Kevin Fauvel, Alessandro Finamore, Lixuan Yang, Fuxing Chen, Dario Rossi
papers.relevance: A leading explainable-by-design traffic classifier; represents the kind of XAI-NTC model whose explanations the attacks in this corpus target, and a hub for the broader corpus.

papers.title: A Survey on Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Internet Traffic Classification and Prediction, and Intrusion Detection
papers.authors: (survey)
papers.relevance: Top-level survey of XAI methods across traffic classification, prediction, and intrusion detection -- the corpus-topic map into which this attack/robustness angle plugs.
